parent_review.original_I137_audit: I140 passes original A137 and R1-R7 without repairs at scope, preserving growing-disk geometry, all normalization/cutoff factors and smooth-remainder arguments. No interface or infinite-volume defect-preserving theorem is inferred. Original I125 canonical-inventory FAIL and separate ordering-only PASS, and original I122 general-Lambda FAIL, remain unchanged.
selected_mathematical_checks: For the unweighted coupled doubling, the two positive scaling exponents solve p beta0=alpha0+2 and q alpha0=beta0+2. Bounded normalized functions give bounded powers even when one exponent is below one; W2r compactness precedes positivity, and strict positivity of the limit restores classical regularity. Positive amplitude coefficients are removed by an invertible log-linear system with determinant 1-pq.

For the annular estimate, the ball of radius |x|/4 around x with |x|<3/4 stays in B1. Rescaling by |x| puts the weight vector uniformly away from zero. The fixed positive bounds and common Holder modulus remain uniform. Thus |x| M(x) is bounded for the weighted gauge; subsequent centers with M tending to infinity approach the origin with bounded pole-to-scale ratio.

Choose n/2<r<n/max(0,-A,-B), with no upper restriction when the maximum is zero. The interval is nonempty because A,B>-2. Moving translated powers are uniformly locally Lr and converge in Lr; bounded normalized components then give W2r compactness and continuous distributional limits through the pole. Strong minimum and coupling exclude a zero component and give positive values also at the pole. This matches the stipulated entire-space solution class.

The Talenti example has fixed smooth coefficients on a ball away from zero and weighted gap positive but unweighted gap zero. It defeats the stated boundary-data-free interior extension, not zero Dirichlet data. The n=3,p=q=4 explicit coefficient profile has fixed value bounds but its Holder seminorm grows at least (8/9) lambda^theta. The p=q=1 sine eigenfunction has exactly zero boundary data and arbitrary amplitude; it is a genuine resonance obstruction.

For V140 the common lower coefficient bound gives coupled mass inequalities; dilation preserves upper/lower bounds and both logarithmic-derivative conditions. Source mass exponents remove the harmonic constants and give uniform truncated-potential estimates. No translation-invariant weighted estimate is used.

The extra virial term has the displayed positive sign on the left of the identity. Its lower bound subtracts delta_b/(q+1) from the f-energy coefficient and delta_a/(p+1) from the g-energy coefficient. Inner boundary terms have orders rho^(n+B) and rho^(n+A), and the coefficient derivative term is bounded by M times finite local energy.

On a retained short interval, the coefficient-weighted endpoint factor has logarithmic derivative bounded by (M+|B|)/q on the annulus. Integration of that derivative controls the ratio to the ideal value, with a constant depending on M. The exact layer integral remains fu/(q+1). Cap, long-interval, high/low-level and localization bounds use positive masses/potentials; their auxiliary parameters can be chosen in the source order with constants uniform over the coefficient class.

The two modified energy coefficients sum to Gamma. Marginal localization absorbs their difference; Gamma>0 implies the original weighted gap is positive. Dilation therefore forces the uniformly bounded local energy to grow by R^(alpha+beta+2-n), contradicting any positive fixed-ball energy.

For the explicit n=3,p=4 profile, the energy and gradient-square integrals converge and the large-sphere Pohozaev terms vanish as a negative power. The integrated radial coefficient term is -1/2 of the nonlinear energy. It obstructs omission of coefficient variation, without claiming sharpness of the pointwise radial budget.

C140 and V140 do not provide a weighted half-space theorem at a boundary pole. Odd reflection loses positivity, while the Dirichlet Green interaction and any harmonic remainder require their own estimates. Neither generic compactness nor an assertion that all constants are uniform supplies the requested quantitative finite-scale bound.
